title: M8: Lagoon Nebula Wide
caption: The Lagoon Nebula (M8), imaged with a 16-inch telescope at Kitt Peak

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: This wide view shows M8, the Lagoon Nebula, a vast region of our galaxy where stars are forming. On a dark night it is easy to spot without any optical aid, just above the spout of the 'teapot' pattern of stars in Sagittarius. Through a small telescope, a milky glow of nebulosity fills the whole field of view.

A star cluster called NGC 6530 shows how star formation is proceeding inside the cloud. A few of its stars appear at the bottom right of this picture, though most of the cluster lies just beyond the frame to the right.

CCD images such as this one hint at how turbulent the nebula's gas is. As new stars form, their strong winds and radiation heat and stir up the material they were born from, sculpting the cloud around them. Regions like the Lagoon are where stars like the Sun are thought to be born.

understand.summary: This is a visible-light image taken with a 16-inch RCOS telescope and CCD camera using several broadband filters. The packet does not say which colour each filter was assigned.
filters: 555 nm · Optical Broad Band (RCOS 16-inch Other CCD)
understand.eye: By eye the Lagoon appears as a faint, milky glow; a long camera exposure brings out its colour and turbulent structure.

alt: A wide field of glowing, turbulent nebulosity with a few cluster stars at the lower right.
